title: Indigenous Kenyan Craft
status: draft: written 18 Nov 2026 offline for Grade 7 Creative Arts and Sports; not yet checked by a CBC Creative Arts and Sports teacher; not loaded by the live tutor
notes: Jewellery belongs to communities; speak with respect. Use local beads and seeds.

skills.key_step: The child says jewellery decorates, shows identity, age and status, marks ceremonies, and names beadwork materials and tools (beads, seeds, thread, wire, needle).

floor.question: What is an age-set?
floor.answer: people initiated at the same time

misconceptions.ask: Which is a material for beadwork?
misconceptions.repair: Sort materials you can thread from those you cannot.

misconceptions.ask: What does jewellery show in Kenyan communities?
misconceptions.repair: Look at pictures of Maasai beadwork: colours show age and status.

misconceptions.ask: Which tool is used for beading?
misconceptions.repair: Thread beads with a needle and show why a hammer would break them.

misconceptions.ask: Do colours in traditional Kenyan beadwork carry meaning?
misconceptions.repair: Read what each colour means in one community.

checks.question: Name one function of jewellery in Kenyan communities.
checks.answer: any of: decoration, identity, status, ceremonies

checks.question: Which tool is used to thread beads?
